en: One liter of liquid water expands to about 1,700 liters of steam when boiled.
Diamond is the hardest natural material, scoring a perfect 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
At 20 degrees Celsius, 100 milliliters of water can dissolve about 200 grams of table sugar.
Water uniquely expands by about nine percent in volume when it freezes into solid ice.
Helium gas is about seven times less dense than the surrounding air, making balloons float.
Solid carbon dioxide, called dry ice, has an extremely cold temperature of minus 78.5 degrees Celsius.
Particles in a true solution are smaller than one nanometer, unlike larger suspension particles.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, melting at exactly 3,422 degrees Celsius.
Gold is extremely dense, with a single cubic meter of solid gold weighing 19,300 kilograms.
Seawater is a mixture containing about 35 grams of dissolved salts per one liter of water.
A single standard drop of water contains approximately 1.5 sextillion water molecules.
Sound travels about 17 times faster in solid steel than in air, reaching 5,960 meters per second.
